title: Hands-On Review: Google Antigravity – The New AI Coding Experiment of 2025
description: A complete hands-on review of Google's new Antigravity AI coding IDE, including setup, features, and comparisons with Cursor, Bolt.new, Replit, and Lovable.
content:
Hands-On Review: Google Antigravity – The New AI Coding Experiment of 2025

Google has once again shaken the developer world by releasing Antigravity, a new AI-powered coding environment that blends intelligent agents, fast reasoning models, and IDE-style workflows. While Google already has tools like Gemini CLI and Jules, Antigravity enters the scene as a public preview — an experiment rather than a final product.

Let’s break down how it performs, how it compares to alternatives like Cursor, Bolt.new, Replit, and Lovable, and whether it’s worth exploring in 2025.

What Is Antigravity?

Antigravity is Google’s experimental AI-assisted IDE, designed to merge:

  • Real-time code suggestions
  • Background agent tasks
  • Project understanding
  • Intelligent refactoring
  • Multi-model AI access

Unlike Gemini CLI, Antigravity is not terminal-based. It's a lightweight editor similar to VS Code but powered by deep AI assistance.

Setup & First Impressions

✔ Smooth Installation

The app installs easily on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

✔ Theme Selection

A simple choice between light and dark mode.

✔ Development Mode Choice

You pick between:

  • Assisted Development: AI helps inside the editor
  • Agentic Mode: Background tasks driven by AI

This shows Google is experimenting with parallel AI workflows, though the feature isn’t fully mature yet.

IDE & Core Features

Once inside, the interface looks almost like VS Code — intentionally familiar. But Antigravity adds advanced AI-powered features:

  • Intelligent Code Understanding — The system scans your entire project and quickly starts suggesting refactors.
  • Smart Fixes & Cleanup — For example, it suggested using Min() and Max() in a messy bounding calculation, a neat, modern improvement.
  • In-Context Edits — Antigravity can apply changes directly into your codebase, with explanations.
  • Strong Model Options — You can choose from different LLMs, including Google’s internal models and Claude Sonnet.

Agent Manager: Promising, But Not Ready

The Agent Manager tries to handle:

  • Task-based conversations
  • Background improvements
  • Semi-autonomous refactoring

However, it currently lacks:

  • True parallel workflows
  • Full branch isolation
  • Smooth UI navigation (panels close often)

Despite these limits, its contextual memory is impressive — it remembers previous improvements and builds on them logically.

Comparison: Antigravity vs Cursor vs Bolt.new vs Replit vs Lovable

To understand Antigravity better, here’s a clear comparison with the most popular AI coding platforms of 2025.

1. Antigravity vs Cursor

Cursor Strengths

  • Best-in-class AI refactoring
  • Extremely accurate project-wide edits
  • Mature agentic workflows
  • Fast search across large codebases
  • Very stable and production-ready

Cursor Weaknesses

  • Heavy on system resources
  • Requires a good GPU/processor for best experience
  • Paid plans are becoming more expensive

Antigravity is not yet as powerful as Cursor. Cursor feels like a battle-tested AI coding tool, while Antigravity feels like a Google experiment. Antigravity’s agentic mode is less polished, but it has the advantage of Google’s ecosystem and future potential.

Verdict: Cursor wins for practical software development today. Antigravity has potential but needs time to mature.

2. Antigravity vs Bolt.new (Bolt AI)

Bolt.new Strengths

  • Browser-based, no installation required
  • Ultra-fast single-file code generation
  • Great for prototypes, small apps, and scripts
  • Fastest “idea → app” tool in the market

Bolt.new Weaknesses

  • Not good for large real projects
  • Limited project understanding
  • No deep multi-file refactoring

Bolt focuses on speed and prototyping, while Antigravity targets IDE-level development with deeper context.

Verdict: Bolt = Build prototypes instantly. Antigravity = Long-term project development (once stable).

3. Antigravity vs Replit

Replit Strengths

  • Cloud-based coding environment
  • One-click hosting & deployment
  • Great for beginners and students
  • Multi-language support
  • AI agents that write full apps

Replit Weaknesses

  • Slower than local IDEs
  • Limited offline capability
  • Code intelligence isn’t as advanced as Cursor or Antigravity

Replit is more of a build-host-deploy platform, while Antigravity is a local AI coding IDE. Choose Replit for collaboration and deployment; choose Antigravity for local, AI-intensive analysis.

4. Antigravity vs Lovable

Lovable Strengths

  • Takes an idea and generates a complete app
  • Clean UI generation
  • Very fast prototyping
  • No coding needed in many cases

Lovable Weaknesses

  • Not ideal for complex enterprise-level apps
  • Generated code often needs manual cleanup
  • Limited long-term maintainability

Lovable creates apps for you, while Antigravity helps you improve apps you build. Lovable suits non-programmers and rapid idea validation; Antigravity targets developers who want structured, AI-assisted refinements.

Final Verdict: Should You Try Antigravity?

Antigravity is exciting but still experimental. It offers:

  • ✔ Strong code reasoning
  • ✔ Impressive contextual understanding
  • ✔ Deep project analysis
  • ✔ Big potential due to Google’s AI ecosystem

But it also needs improvements in:

  • ✘ Task automation
  • ✘ UI flow
  • ✘ Parallel agent workflows
  • ✘ Stability

Recommendation: Try it now, watch it closely, and revisit after a few updates.
